summary: Tested new public hotel website (frontend) + public_routes.py backend endpoints. 11/11 backend tests pass. Full booking flow (search → results → guest details → payment summary with 5-min countdown timer) works end-to-end. Website redirects / → /website, CRM login still works at /dashboard. Fixed one tz-naive vs tz-aware datetime bug in get_booking_status.

minor.issue: Was returning 500 due to comparing naive datetime from Mongo with timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc). Fixed by normalizing expires_at to UTC-aware before comparison in public_routes.py line ~479.

issues: Room card has a 'BOOK NOW' button at top-right of each result card (data-testid absent) and a 'Select' button at right. Two near-identical actions could be confusing. Consider consolidating OR add data-testid='select-room-btn' on the Select button for better testability.
Cloudflare Turnstile shows 'Unable to connect to website' on the preview domain (expected per task note). Contact submit still works when secret missing or network error (bypass in code).

action_items: Review the datetime timezone fix in public_routes.py get_booking_status (normalize expires_at tzinfo). Consider applying same pattern defensively in any future code that reads datetimes back from Mongo.
Optional: add data-testid='select-room-btn' to Website.js step-2 room cards for easier automated testing.
No further action required to ship the website MVP; PayHere sandbox credentials still placeholder per task note.
critical_code_review_comments: public_routes.py line 234-235: check_in/check_out are stored as naive datetimes (strptime), while expires_at is tz-aware. Mongo stores both; on retrieval both are naive. The server-side filter {expires_at: $gt: now} works because Mongo normalizes to UTC, but Python-side comparisons must be careful. Applied fix in get_booking_status; consider doing same in cleanup_expired_holds / get_held_rooms_for_dates (currently fine because comparisons happen in Mongo).

public_routes.py line 282: `'sandbox' in os.environ.get('PAYHERE_BASE_URL', 'sandbox')` evaluates sandbox flag against the URL string; works but a dedicated PAYHERE_SANDBOX bool env var would be cleaner.

public_routes.py payhere/notify endpoint has no idempotency guard – if PayHere retries notifications, duplicate bookings/customers could be created. Suggest checking existing booking by order_id/payment_id before insert.
Website.js booking engine lacks 'nights < 1' client-side validation beyond date auto-fix. Backend handles it but UX could show inline error.
No HTTP 429/rate-limit protection on public endpoints (contact / availability / hold). Potential abuse surface.

rca of the issue: Bug: GET /api/public/booking/status/{order_id} returned 500 with TypeError 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes'. Reproduction: POST /api/public/booking/hold then GET /api/public/booking/status/{returned_order_id}. Root cause: hold_record.expires_at written as timezone-aware (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta), but MongoDB BSON strips tzinfo on round-trip, so the retrieved value is naive. Line 480 did `now > expires_at` with aware now vs naive expires_at. Mitigation: Normalize expires_at by applying .replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) before comparison. Alternative long-term: enforce consistent tz handling across all datetime fields when writing/reading from Mongo.
